scenes.heading: Simple interest
scenes.say: Put money in a bank and the bank pays you interest. Borrow money and you pay interest. The simplest kind is simple interest, where the interest is the same every single year.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A tenant pays you the same rent every week
scenes.science: The bank pays the same interest every year
scenes.breaks: Interest is a percentage, so more money earns more. Real accounts usually compound.
scenes.say: Think of interest as rent for your money. A tenant pays the same rent every week they stay. With simple interest, the bank pays you the same amount every year it keeps your money. But interest is a percentage, so a bigger deposit earns more.

scenes.heading: The simple interest formula
parts: rate per year, as a decimal
scenes.say: I equals P times r times t. I is the interest. P is the principal, the starting amount. r is the yearly rate, as a decimal, so five per cent is point zero five. And t is the time, in years. The total amount at the end is P plus I.
scenes.caption: I = P × r × t. I is the interest. P is the principal. r is the yearly rate as a decimal, so 5% is 0.05. t is the time in years. The total amount is A = P + I.

scenes.heading: Equal steps every year
scenes.say: Here's two thousand dollars at five per cent simple interest. First the starting bar, two thousand. Each year adds five per cent of two thousand, which is one hundred dollars. The steps are all the same size, so after five years you have two thousand five hundred.
scenes.caption: $2000 at 5% simple interest. Each year adds 5% of $2000 = $100. The steps are all equal, so after 5 years you have $2500.

scenes.heading: Months to years
scenes.question: Find the simple interest on $3600 at 4.5% p.a. for 8 months.
scenes.say: Find the interest on three thousand six hundred dollars at four point five per cent for eight months. The rate is per year, so change eight months to years: two thirds. Then three thousand six hundred, times point zero four five, times two thirds, is one hundred and eight dollars.
scenes.caption: Find the interest on $3600 at 4.5% p.a. for 8 months. Change 8 months to years: ⅔. Then 3600 × 0.045 × ⅔ = $108.

scenes.heading: Finding the rate
scenes.question: $5000 earns $900 simple interest in 3 years. Find the rate.
scenes.say: Five thousand dollars earns nine hundred in three years. What's the rate? Rearrange: r equals I divided by P times t. Nine hundred divided by fifteen thousand is point zero six. That's six per cent per year.
scenes.caption: $5000 earns $900 in 3 years. Rearrange: r = I ÷ (P × t). 900 ÷ 15 000 = 0.06, which is 6% p.a.

Rearrange to find P, r or t
scenes.say: Quick recap. I equals P r t, with the rate as a decimal and the time in years. The total amount is the principal plus the interest. Simple interest is the same every year. And you can rearrange the formula to find any missing value. Now try the practice questions!
